We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+xy\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
html:
We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius 2 centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as

r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj,0≤t≤π2.

So, along the curve C, we have x=2cos⁡t,y=2sin⁡t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+xyj=2cos⁡ti+2cos⁡t⋅2sin⁡tj=2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(2sin⁡t)j=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj)⋅(−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj)=2cos⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+4cos⁡tsin⁡t⋅2cos⁡t=−4sin⁡tcos⁡t+8sin⁡tcos2⁡t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫0π/2F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt.
